pointers.sentence: `EmailMessage.__init__` takes the subject, the body, the sender and the To list by position or by name, and the rest by name only (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.__init__`).
Passing any argument after the first four by position warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` (6.0; `django/utils/deprecation.py:deprecate_posargs`).
A backend given as `connection=`, and the `EmailMessage.connection` property, are deprecated in 6.1 in favour of an alias of `MAILERS` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

They warn only when the caller is outside Django, so `EmailMultiAlternatives`, which passes the connection on to `EmailMessage.__init__`, gives no warning (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

`EmailMessage.message` makes an empty `email.message.EmailMessage` under the policy it is given, `email.policy.default` unless the caller names another, and fills it in a fixed order (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`):

The identifier comes from `email.utils.make_msgid` with the domain `DNS_NAME`, a `CachedDnsName`, which asks `socket.getfqdn` for the machine's name when first needed and keeps it, as the lookup can take seconds and slow the server's restart, its comment says (`django/core/mail/utils.py:CachedDnsName`).

Unless the policy allows UTF-8 in headers, as neither `email.policy.default` nor `email.policy.SMTP` does, a domain outside ASCII in an address header is rewritten in its IDNA form; the comment cites CPython issue 83938, in which the email package would write it as an RFC 2047 encoded word (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage._idna_encode_address_header_domains`).

A header is parsed as it is set, and a value that a carriage return, a line feed or another line boundary splits into more than one line raises `ValueError`, on which Django's protection against header injection relies, its documentation says (`docs/topics/email.txt`).

A subject with a newline inside it makes an `EmailMessage` without complaint and fails when the message is built, which the local-memory backend does at the send for that alone (`django/core/mail/backends/locmem.py:EmailBackend.send_messages`).
`EmailMessage.message` returns an `email.message.EmailMessage` of the modern API (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

Deprecated with the change, to go in Django 2028: the legacy classes it built, `SafeMIMEText` and `SafeMIMEMultipart`; the helpers `forbid_multi_line_headers` and `sanitize_address`; attachments of the legacy `email.mime.base.MIMEBase`; and `BadHeaderError`, now `ValueError` itself so that code catching it catches what the modern API raises, its comment says (`django/core/mail/message.py:BadHeaderError`).
`EmailMessage.recipients` returns the To, Cc and Bcc lists joined, empty entries left out (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.recipients`).

The SMTP backend gives the server `recipients` as the envelope's recipients and `EmailMessage.from_email` as its sender, whatever the headers say (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend._send`).
`EmailMessage.send` returns what the backend's `send_messages` returns, the number sent (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).
`EmailMessage.attach` takes an attachment in one of two forms, besides the deprecated `email.mime.base.MIMEBase` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.attach`).
It decodes text again, its comment says, for attachments put into `EmailMessage.attachments` without `attach` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage._add_attachment`).

`EmailMultiAlternatives` is an `EmailMessage` with a list of other versions of its body, `EmailMultiAlternatives.alternatives`, each an `EmailAlternative` of a content and a type, added with `EmailMultiAlternatives.attach_alternative` or given to the constructor (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMultiAlternatives.attach_alternative`).

`send_mail`, `mail_admins` and `mail_managers` build their messages with it, and attach as an alternative the HTML they are given (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`, `django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).

`send_mail`, `mail_admins` and `mail_managers` build their messages with it, and attach as an alternative the HTML they are given (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`, `django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).
When the message is built, only the body is added differently (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMultiAlternatives._add_bodies`).

`EmailMultiAlternatives.body_contains` is true when a text is in the plain body and in every alternative of a text type, which its documentation says can be useful in tests (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMultiAlternatives.body_contains`, `docs/topics/email.txt`).
